submissions.title: Boise City Council approves 6-month moratorium on large data center construction
submissions.excerpt: applies to all data center projects that are 100,000 square-feet or larger, or use 20 megawatts of power
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Boise, ID city council unanimously approved an immediate 6-month moratorium (effective Nov 10, 2026) on new applications for large data centers (>=100,000 sq ft OR >=20 MW), proposed by Mayor Lauren McLean, while the city studies water, energy/grid, wastewater, noise and public-safety impacts. Not tied to a specific tracked project in the database (no Boise-area project currently tracked); this is a citywide policy restriction, so left unlinked rather than guessed. Multiple consistent outlets (East Idaho News, Washington State Standard, Idaho News) corroborate the date and vote.

submissions.title: Microsoft exits Nscale's 50MW Loughton data center deal in Essex
submissions.excerpt: Microsoft had ended its anchor agreement for the 50MW facility
submissions.note: Status-change flag for tracked project 'Nscale Loughton' (Essex, UK; currently ANNOUNCED, 90MW scalable ceiling / 50MW initial per tracker, last verified 2026-07-28 -- i.e. BEFORE this event, so likely not yet reflected). Multiple outlets (City A.M., The Sun, CTV News, Baxtel, MobileWorldLive) report Microsoft withdrew as anchor tenant around Oct 18-19, 2026, reportedly because UK Power Networks could not supply grid power to the site on Nscale's timeline (one outlet cites early-to-mid 2030s). Nscale says it remains 'committed' to the site and is exploring alternative power sources; Microsoft called it specific to 'a single site,' not the wider partnership. This comes as Nscale pursues a reported NY IPO.
